label: final copy output of length-3 sequences (plus weak late-copy tail)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never on original tokens or <DEL>, and only from recall_idx >= 2. The clean, high-magnitude part is the last step of length-3 sequences (t=5, input orig(1), output orig(2)): about 87% precision, 43% of activation mass, and nearly all of the top-quartile activations (e.g. q p k <DEL> q [p]). The rest is a diffuse, low-magnitude tail on the last one or two copy steps (to_go <= 1) of longer sequences, at only a few percent of such steps. It is biased toward certain input tokens (l, q, p, n, f, 3, z, u) but no simple rule captures it: the best disjunction I tried reaches mass recall 0.79 at precision only 0.15. It does not fire on recall_idx 0-1, on early copy steps with 6 or more outputs left, or on any original-phase step. Magnitude is largest at L=3 t=5 and is modulated by input token identity there (f, q, p strongest; v, c, g, y often below threshold).
